subject_matter: Value — the concept space of value in philosophical discourse: the good in itself, the instrumental, the posited, the fitting, the valid
source: Aristotle, Nicomachean Ethics I.7; Moore, Principia Ethica (1903); Dewey, Theory of Valuation (1939); Marx, Capital I ch. 1 (use value); Nietzsche, On the Genealogy of Morals (Wertsetzung); Heidegger, 'Nietzsche's Word: God is Dead'; Brentano, The Origin of our Knowledge of Right and Wrong (1889); Scheler, Formalism in Ethics (1913); Scanlon, What We Owe to Each Other (1998); Weber, 'Science as a Vocation' (1919); Habermas, The Theory of Communicative Action (1981); Kant, Groundwork

signature.meaning: the first is chosen or valued for the sake of the second
the first posits the second as a value (a valuation sets it)
the first merits the second (a fitting attitude, a correct love)
the first binds the second (an ought, a validity claim that obliges)
the first holds independently of the second
